scope: Real Debian controller, unprivileged trusted manager, LUKS profiles and dedicated session VM lifecycle with synthetic data. Compiled OpenCode chat TUI, without component redesign.

jobs.name: x86 host LUKS and manager lifecycle

checks.network_matrix_detail: 12 SOCKS and 9 offline Tor cases; detailed earlier packet-capture report remains transport-vm-evidence.json.

host_runtime.scope: real LUKS/systemd/QEMU lifecycle with synthetic data; nested TCG is NOT an isolation guarantee
host_runtime.workload: systemd service crash/recovery with real manager and VM
checks: PASS: interrupted general filesystem formatting retains an unpublished file and retry never overwrites it
PASS: recovery latches before a busy operation lock and only verified closure clears it
PASS: systemd waits for controller readiness and runs the confined manager as UID 1000
PASS: fragmented controller frames and secrets expire despite continued progress; the same service accepts the next valid request
PASS: outer disk exhaustion cannot publish a partial general volume; explicit cleanup permits retry
PASS: trusted setup confirms discard, recreates a complete general volume and protects existing archives
PASS: trusted manager saves a hidden API key only in the root-owned encrypted profile; status and manager UID cannot retrieve it
PASS: trusted network menu saves hidden proxy credentials only in the root-owned encrypted profile; offline policy refuses external proxies
PASS: temporary transport stays in RAM; saved selection restores it; unknown fields, aliases and corrupt profiles never trigger a fallback
PASS: full-disk transport update preserves the prior profile; retry replaces the interrupted private staging file
PASS: invalid keys and staging aliases are rejected; an interrupted private staging file permits an atomic retry
PASS: legacy key is read without migration; ENOSPC preserves it and retry publishes the versioned archive before deleting the legacy file
PASS: full-disk replacement preserves the archive; published archives take precedence over leftover legacy secrets and malformed archives fail closed
PASS: key persists across lock/unlock; removal requires confirmation and cancellation preserves it
PASS: trusted manager adds and renames a second hidden key, saves its default and selects another key only in RAM
PASS: active chat blocks persistent, temporary and saved-profile transport changes
PASS: key picker chooses the opening credential; an active session blocks key mutations and identity changes
PASS: removing the selected key never rotates to the remaining account; explicit default and selection restore access
PASS: read-only transport choices use RAM, clear on lock and leave the entire encrypted image byte-identical
PASS: read-only profile exposes key metadata and permits RAM selection, rejects all key mutations and pending deletion, and remains byte-identical
PASS: interrupted session formatting survives restart, cannot open, and is discarded only after confirmation
PASS: disk exhaustion is explicit, preserves existing archives and permits reopening after pending cleanup
PASS: SIGKILL of manager powers down the VM and closes both LUKS mappings before restarting
PASS: SIGKILL of controller stops its dependent manager and recovers before both restart
PASS: unresponsive VM leaves recovery latched and rejects every new opening
PASS: recovery survives restart; cancelled force-stop preserves VM; explicit confirmation closes both volumes
PASS: controller stop drains dependent services and leaves no active VM or open volume
PASS: synthetic passwords, API keys and proxy credentials never appear on the managed console

earlier_attempts: host-transport-ci-evidence.json preserves the partial ARM host runs and direct boot investigation.

ci_setup_corrections.reason: Use opencode-linux-x64-baseline as the build target; cli-linux-x64-baseline is the output directory.
Activate the runner user membership with sg kvm for every VM command; sudo with an alternate run-as group required a password on this runner.

limits: The outer x86 Debian laboratory uses KVM; the actual session VM still uses the explicit lab-only TCG backend. Production session KVM isolation is not verified.
The profile/UI suite has no gateway VM. It verifies selection, persistence, secrecy, recovery and refusal during an open session, but not an actual host-managed Tor/SOCKS switch or provider request.
Real Abliteration, active-stream global shutdown, tools proxy, file transfers, full ephemeral guest and physical USB/live image remain roadmap gates.
Console dimensions are fixed at 100x30 for the host and 100x27 for the chat fixture; narrow/wide menus and physical console behavior require separate coverage.
Synthetic canary absence on this laboratory disk and console is a scoped test, not a proof that every possible data trace is absent.
ARM64 direct chat boot and the separate ARM64 network matrix pass; the double-TCG ARM host lifecycle timeout remains documented and is not reclassified as success.
